purpose: Source-supported exact-sense and Myanmar-language triage; NOT independent verification or approval
source_limitations: Publisher pages accessed via public search indexing; some direct requests returned HTTP 403. Treat publisher labels as indexed evidence leads, never as independent exact-sense human signoff. Cambridge grammar page for quite supplies no CEFR rating.

records.sense: information reported or inferred but not established as certain
records.risk: B1 draft versus Cambridge-indexed B2 for matching reported-information sense
records.proposed_burmese: ကြားသိရသလောက်၊ သိရသည့်အရ (သေချာမအတည်ပြုရသေး)
records.proposed_example: Apparently, the delivery has been delayed until Friday.
records.english_definition: According to what seems true or what people have said.
records.burmese_meaning: ကြားသိရသည့်အရ၊ ထင်ရသလောက်
records.example_sentence: Apparently, the meeting has been moved to Friday.

records.sense: extremely important to an outcome, not 'disapproving' or 'gravely ill'
records.risk: B1 draft versus Cambridge-indexed B2 for the exact importance sense
records.proposed_burmese: ရလဒ်အတွက် အလွန်အရေးပါသော၊ အဆုံးအဖြတ်ပေးနိုင်သော
records.proposed_example: A reliable water supply is critical during an emergency.
records.english_definition: Extremely important for success or safety.
records.burmese_meaning: အလွန်အရေးကြီးသော၊ မရှိမဖြစ်လိုအပ်သော
records.example_sentence: Clean drinking water is critical during an emergency.

records.sense: somewhat / to a modest degree, with context-sensitive emphasis
records.risk: A2 draft versus Cambridge-indexed B1; draft 'noticeable degree, often more than expected' may overstate intensity
records.proposed_burmese: အတော်လေး၊ နည်းနည်း (အခြေအနေအလိုက် အလေးပေးမှုကွာနိုင်)
records.proposed_example: The instructions were rather difficult to follow.
records.english_definition: To a noticeable degree, often more than expected.
records.burmese_meaning: အတော်လေး၊ ထင်ထားသည်ထက်ပို၍
records.example_sentence: The instructions were rather difficult to follow.

records.sense: sunny and dry weather, chiefly British English
records.source_heading: fine adjective (SUNNY) versus fine adjective (SATISFACTORY) A1
records.risk: Draft definition describes satisfactory A1 sense while its weather example more naturally invokes sunny/dry B1 sense; exact sense, definition, example and level do not align
records.proposed_example: The weather stayed fine and dry throughout the picnic.
records.english_definition: Good enough or acceptable in quality.
records.burmese_meaning: အဆင်ပြေသော၊ လက်ခံနိုင်လောက်သော
records.example_sentence: The weather was fine for our picnic.

records.sense: warning about what follows if advice is not taken
records.source_heading: otherwise conjunction (CONSEQUENCE) B1 versus otherwise adverb (NOT INCLUDING) B2
records.risk: Draft marks adverb, while Cambridge labels this exact conditional connector as conjunction; human grammar/POS adjudication required
records.proposed_burmese: မဟုတ်လျှင်၊ ထိုသို့မလုပ်ပါက
records.proposed_example: Hurry up; otherwise, we will miss the train.
records.english_definition: If not; used to explain what will happen without a particular action.
records.burmese_meaning: မဟုတ်လျှင်၊ သို့မဟုတ်ပါက
records.example_sentence: Leave now; otherwise, you may miss the train.

records.sense: contrastive sentence connector, not degree construction 'however hard'
records.source_heading: however adverb (COMPARING) A2 versus degree construction B2
records.risk: Draft A2 contrast sense has indexed support; ensure future review does not transfer B2 degree label to the contrastive sense
records.proposed_burmese: သို့သော်၊ ဒါပေမဲ့ (ရှေ့ဝါကျနှင့် ဆန့်ကျင်သည့်အချက်ကို ဆက်ပြောရာတွင်)
records.proposed_example: The room was small; however, it was comfortable.
records.english_definition: Used to introduce a fact that contrasts with what was just said.
records.example_sentence: The room was small; however, it was comfortable.

records.sense: for that reason, expressing logical consequence
records.risk: Draft B1 sense appears aligned; preserve distinction from contrastive however and conditional otherwise
records.proposed_example: The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.
records.english_definition: For that reason; as a result.
records.example_sentence: The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.

records.sense: moderately with gradable adjective, but completely with non-gradable adjective
records.source_heading: Quite — Cambridge English Grammar Today (not a CEFR-rated headword page)
records.risk: Draft 'fairly large degree but not completely' is too categorical; quite can mean completely with non-gradable adjectives; this grammar page gives NO CEFR level
records.proposed_burmese: အတော်လေး (အတိုင်းအတာရှိသော adjective များနှင့်)၊ လုံးဝ (အပြည့်အဝဖြစ်သော adjective များနှင့်)
records.english_definition: To a fairly large degree, but not completely.
